article_title: Supporting workforce practice change: protocol for a pilot study of a motivational interviewing virtual client software tool for health professionals.
citation: Oster Candice, Schoo Adrian, Litt John, Morello Andrea, Leibbrandt Richard, Antonello Christopher, Powers David, Lange Belinda, Maeder Anthony, Lawn Sharon. (2020). Supporting workforce practice change: protocol for a pilot study of a motivational interviewing virtual client software tool for health professionals. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2019-033080
title: V-CCT: a virtual client conversation tool for practising motivational interviewing
description: The V-CCT is a website-based conversation tool for teaching MI, built around a virtual client case study named Anna focused on diet and weight loss. It uses "a hybrid of classes two and three" of interactive virtual clients: the user types a question or response, then selects the closest match from a restricted set of options, and the client replies in text form. The dialogue is modelled in an SQL database that generates the client's response and four multiple-choice options each turn, and each conversation attempt is logged with date and time for retrospective analysis.
requirements: Users access the tool via a website and enter either a precourse dialogue (before the MI course) or a postcourse dialogue (after the course)
The user types a question/response and then selects the closest match from a restricted set of responses each turn
constraints: VC responses are text form only in the pilot version, with an avatar planned for the next stage of the project
No feedback is provided during the conversation flow in the pilot version, and users are not shown which responses are MI-consistent
target_learners: Postgraduate health professional students (medicine, nursing, psychology, physiotherapy, nutrition and dietetics, occupational therapy)
target_learning_goals: Develop, practise and receive feedback on motivational interviewing skills for supporting client behavioural change
examples: Users are introduced to the virtual client Anna in a short video, then converse with her about behavioural change relating to diet and exercise before and after completing the online MI course
